Keep compatibility_date current

Set compatibility_date to a recent date so the Worker can use current runtime APIs. This article explains how wrangler.jsonc should declare it, and why a stale date silently disables newer bindings.

Example

Put the date next to the compatibility flags. Node.js built-ins still need nodejs_compat. Paid plans should raise cpu_ms instead of hoping the default 10 ms Free budget will extract an article. 

{
  "compatibility_date": "2026-09-19",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "limits": { "cpu_ms": 30000 }
}

Checklist

  • Bump compatibility_date when you adopt a 2026 runtime API.
  • Keep nodejs_compat if the Worker imports node:buffer.
  • Read the compatibility dates notes before shipping.

The devil is in the details: a Worker that still pins 2024-01-01 will reject Durable Object SQLite calls even when the account is on Workers Paid.
